title: Measure neighboring guide retention rather than infer jamming from average wash yield
statement: For a final site blocked only by two retained guides, jam probability is their joint retention probability. Marginals q_i,q_j give max(0,q_i+q_j-1)<=P(both retained)<=min(q_i,q_j). Independent identical clearance r gives no-jam1-(1-r)^2; perfectly correlated within-pair failures give only r. Raising either motif probability to K additionally requires independence across motifs.

requires: Joint retained-guide events at the final challenge; any independence within pairs or across motifs must be separately supplied.
Four-cohort interpretation additionally needs common exposure, homogeneous first-order kinetics and0<p_x<1.

body: The jam event is the intersection of two retention events; Frechet bounds follow from containment and inclusion-exclusion. At r=.9, independent-pair no-jam is.99 but common-mode pair no-jam is.9. The100-motif products in the source additionally assume motifs independent; a shared global failure across motifs cannot be replaced by those products. This concerns the retained pair at the final challenge, not an acquired dynamic wash process. Chemical cleavage of a donor linkage does not imply physical duplex ejection or restored access; hydrolyzed and trapped strands also need clearance. A proposed four-cohort assay presets neither/A/B/AB products, challenges C at common t, and under homogeneous first-order kinetics uses k_x=-ln(1-p_x)/t and eta=1-k_AB*k0/(k_A*k_B). Positive eta rejects the specified multiplicative-inhibition null, not uniquely steric causation; electrostatics, salt/density and competing nucleophiles are confounders. Require0<p_x<1,t>0 and measured product identity, then test selective guide displacement or an alternate C approach.
